questions.q: This lesson and Chapter 8 both use DMVs. What's the actual difference between them?
options: Same tool, different purpose — this lesson uses DMVs for monitoring (is the system healthy right now), while Chapter 8 uses DMVs to diagnose why one specific query is slow
This lesson's DMVs only work on Azure SQL, while Chapter 8's only work on-prem
There is no difference — the two chapters cover identical content
Chapter 8 doesn't use DMVs at all, only Extended Events
questions.explain: DMVs are reused across the course for different jobs — monitoring here, query-plan diagnosis in Chapter 8's dedicated deep dive.

questions.q: What does filtering sys.dm_exec_sessions with WHERE is_user_process = 1 accomplish?
options: It drops SQL Server's own internal system sessions, leaving only real client/user activity
It deletes all sessions from the server immediately
It shows only sessions that have caused a deadlock
It filters the results to only Azure Managed Instance targets
questions.explain: Without that filter, the results would be cluttered with SQL Server's own background/system sessions.

questions.q: What makes sys.dm_db_resource_stats different from a typical on-prem SQL Server DMV, per this lesson?
options: It's specific to Azure SQL Database and doesn't exist on-prem, because on-prem SQL Server has no provisioned-tier concept to report utilization against
It only works when connected via SSMS, never Azure Data Studio
It requires a paid Azure Monitor license to query
It returns data from every database in the entire subscription at once
questions.explain: This DMV reports resource consumption relative to a provisioned tier (DTU/vCore), a concept that only exists in Azure SQL Database.

questions.q: Roughly how much history and at what sampling interval does sys.dm_db_resource_stats return data?
options: One row every 15 seconds, covering roughly the last hour
One row per year, going back a decade
It returns only a single current snapshot with no history at all
One row every 24 hours for the past week
questions.explain: This gives a rolling window of recent CPU/IO/memory utilization history, useful for confirming a baseline or spotting a recent spike.

questions.q: Why does this lesson deliberately exclude execution-plan and index-usage DMVs from the DBA's monitoring set?
options: Because those DMVs answer "why is this specific query slow," which is a query-tuning question covered in Chapter 8, not a monitoring question
Because execution-plan DMVs don't exist in SQL Server
Because they require a different licensing tier than monitoring DMVs
Because they can only be queried once every 24 hours
questions.explain: This lesson focuses on "is the system healthy right now" monitoring; query-plan diagnosis gets its own deep dive later in the course.
